subject: MSA / Order Form — UX component titleing and downstream-use guardrails for AI-derived outputs
messages:
From: Diane Kerr <diane.kerr@vectra.io>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Huang <alex.huang@vectra.io>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on title / downstream-use language (MSA + Order Form)

Diego,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our product team is enthusiastic. Legal had a few follow-up questions after reviewing the draft MSA + Order Form. They want to be explicit about two items before we can approve:

1) "Title" for outputs that the customer uses inside their product (widgets, canned responses, generated UX text). We need to ensure Vectra can claim product title to the generated assets for internal UX flows and not be exposed to any assignment that would let Redwood re-use or re-train on those artifacts without consent.

2) Downstream productization limits — our procurement team wants a clear carveout that allows Vectra to ship features that embed the model output into our proprietary interfaces, but disallows Redwood from incorporating Vectra-specific prompts or outputs back into model training without an explicit opt-in.

Can you confirm whether the redlines you provided yesterday cover both points and, if not, propose specific language? We can loop in our counsel (Alex) and aim to close by end of next week.

Appreciate it —
Diane
Legal Operations, Vectra

[Attachment: walkthrough-screens-annotated.pdf]

From: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Diane Kerr <diane.kerr@vectra.io>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on title / downstream-use language (MSA + Order Form)

Diane — thanks for the clear notes and the annotated screenshots. Short answer: yes, the intent of our existing redline addresses both, but legal/ops feedback yesterday flagged that the wording could be tighter on (1) explicit title for customer-facing in-product assets and (2) a non-ambiguous opt-out for training.

Next steps from our side:
- Monica (Contracts) will propose precise sentence-level language for the Order Form that explicitly assigns title for "Customer-generated UI artifacts and packaged outputs" to Vectra.
- Laura (Legal) will add a clear negative covenant preventing Redwood from using Vectra-specific prompts/outputs for model training or benchmarking unless Vectra provides written consent (opt-in checkbox on the Order Form).

I'll drop a draft by end of day Friday for your review. If you want faster turnaround, we can do a quick 30-minute call Thu morning.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0124

[References: redline_proposal_20270310.docx (internal)]

From: monica.patel@redwood.ai <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft language for title & training opt-in (for DF to share)

Diego / Laura — Pasting two short clauses below that I think will map cleanly into the Order Form and MSA exhibits. I've kept the language modular so legal can choose to put it in Order Form, Exhibit A, or an appendix.

1) Customer Output Title Clause (Order Form) — "Customer shall retain exclusive title to Customer-Generated Outputs: all textual, graphical, and packaged UX artifacts produced by the Service using Customer prompts or data ("Customer-Generated Outputs"). Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use such Outputs in Customer's internal and commercial products as described in the Order Form."

2) Training and Feedback Opt-In (MSA Exhibit) — "Redwood will only use Customer prompts, Customer-Generated Outputs, or other Customer-provided non-public data for model training, benchmarking, or service improvements if Customer has explicitly opted in by written agreement or the dedicated opt-in selection on the applicable Order Form. Unless and until such opt-in is provided, Redwood shall not incorporate Customer prompts or outputs into any model weights, training corpora, or public benchmarks."

Notes: I did not include a carve that prevents Redwood from collecting telemetry (counts/latency/aggregate metrics) — we consider that operational, not training data. If Vectra wants telemetry excluded entirely we can add limited language, but that may affect our ability to support them.

If that looks ok, Diego — please share with Diane and Alex and request any targeted edits.

-Monica
Senior Contracts Counsel, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redline_proposal_20270311.docx]

From: Diane Kerr <diane.kerr@vectra.io>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Huang <alex.huang@vectra.io>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 10:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft language for title & training opt-in (for DF to share)

Monica, Diego — thanks, that is helpful and closer to what our counsel needs. A few quick comments from our side:

- The Customer Output Title clause looks fine, but we need a short clarifier in the Order Form that "Customer-Generated Outputs" includes derivatives that Vectra creates by combining model outputs with their proprietary enrichment layers (e.g., labeling, ranking).
- On Training and Feedback Opt-In, Alex asked whether "telemetry" can be scoped more clearly — we can accept collection of anonymized metrics but want an explicit exclusion for any prompts, prompt templates, or output logs that can be reverse-engineered to reconstruct customer prompts.

Could you add a single-sentence clarification under the Title clause and tweak the opt-in clause to call out "aggregate telemetry allowed; prompt and output logs excluded unless redacted or consented"? If you can send that redline we can run it by our procurement counsel.

Thanks —
Diane

On Fri, Mar 12, 2027 at 08:29 AM diego.fernandez@redwood.ai wrote:
> Diane — quick follow. Monica attached a proposed doc; I can add the clarifier you suggest.
> 
> Diego

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Diane Kerr <diane.kerr@vectra.io>, diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft language for title & training opt-in (for DF to share)

Diane / Alex / Diego — attaching an updated redline that implements your clarifier and tightens the telemetry language as requested. Key changes:

- Definition expanded: "'Customer-Generated Outputs' includes Derivative Outputs defined as Customer-produced assets that incorporate or transform Service outputs together with Customer proprietary enrichment, labeling, or ranking logic."
- Training prohibition refined: "Redwood may collect and use anonymized, aggregated telemetry (e.g., token counts, latency distributions, error rates) for performance monitoring and product improvement. Redwood will not, without Customer's explicit written opt-in, retain or use raw prompts, prompt templates, or model outputs that are linkable to Customer identities or could be reasonably reconstructed into Customer prompts for the purpose of model training or benchmarking."

I've flagged two optional edits in the document where parties sometimes negotiate: (a) a limited 30-day post-deployment feedback window where customers can opt to allow temporary debugging access to output logs under NDA; (b) a committal to a quarterly review cadence for telemetry retention policies. Either is optional; we recommend keeping both if Vectra expects heavy integration.

Please review the attached redline (redline_proposal_20270314.docx) and let me know if we should set up a call to finalize. If you approve, Diego — please confirm and we'll ask Legal Ops to incorporate into the final Order Form.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

[Attachment: redline_proposal_20270314.docx]
